title: quercus brachyphylla subsp. brevifolia
intro: Quercus brachyphylla subsp. brevifolia, commonly known as the Guanacaste oak, is a subspecies of evergreen tree native to Mexico. This plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, offering health benefits such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects, which may help in reducing the risk of chronic diseases like cancer, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. The therapeutic actions of Guanacaste oak include its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce oxidative stress, and exhibit analgesic and antipyretic properties. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
